newsitem.title: USA: Electrocution caused Florida mystery horse deaths.
newsitem.headline: Electrocution caused Florida mystery horse deaths.

text.p: Police said on Tuesday they had figured out why two police horses mysteriously dropped dead on the same spot in downtown Orlando one week apart. They were electrocuted.

Mounted officer Louie Rodriguez was riding his horse Cheyenne by a state building on Sunday when the horse was stricken. Cheyenne bolted about three feet (one metre) and dropped down dead, Rodriguez said.
Veterinarians thought it was a heart attack until Rodriguez recalled that another police mount, Panthers Pride, had died of an apparent heart attack a week earlier on the same spot.

Wayne Zimmerman, an electrical engineer for the Orlando Utilities Commission, said on Tuesday both horses had been electrocuted through a combination of wet grass, metal horse shoes and faulty wiring.

Zimmerman said faulty wiring leaking from underground wires sent a current into the soil. The charge was not strong enough to hurt a person. But a horse with two front legs planted on the strongly positive charge and its rear legs planted in a negatively charged area would be large enough to complete the circuit and cause electrocution.
Metal horse shoes would conduct electricity better than the leather or rubber soles most people wear, he added.
